name: fsck
description: Checks and repairs Linux filesystems for errors. Run it on UNMOUNTED filesystems only.

flags.description: Check without repairing (report only) on most filesystems.
Answer yes to every repair question (use with care).
Check all filesystems in /etc/fstab (what boot does).
Show what would be done without doing it.

examples.explanation: Read-only check: reports errors without fixing them.
The correct sequence: unmount, then repair with automatic yes.
Forces a full check even if the filesystem was marked clean.

about: fsck is a front end that dispatches to filesystem-specific checkers (fsck.ext4, fsck.xfs). ext4 repairs are interactive-capable; XFS uses xfs_repair instead, since fsck.xfs is a stub that does nothing. Modern ext4/xfs journals make manual fsck rare — it mostly matters after power loss on non-journaled filesystems or real corruption.
useCases: Verify a disk before trusting it again.
Fix filesystems flagged dirty at boot.
mistakes: Running fsck on a MOUNTED filesystem — it corrupts data. Unmount first (except for / at early boot).
Expecting fsck.xfs to repair — use xfs_repair for XFS.
warnings: Repairing with -y on a failing disk can make things worse; image the disk first (ddrescue) when data matters.
